h1: Your Team Answered That Question Yesterday
seo_title: Why Customers Ask the Same Questions and How to Fix the Cause | NATA
meta_description: Follow a repeated customer question through sales and operations. See when to clarify the offer, send a status update, or keep the decision with a person.
section_questions: Why do customers ask a question that’s already answered?
When is a repeated question really a request for a status update?
Which repeated questions should stay with a person?
How do you find the cause inside your own business?
answer_capsule: Customers keep asking the same question when the answer is missing, hard to find, out of date, or unclear at the moment they need it. Sometimes the answer depends on a decision someone still has to make. Trace one inquiry back to what the customer saw and what they needed to do next. That tells you whether to clarify the offer, update a job’s status, or put someone in charge of the decision.
takeaways: Find the exact place where the customer needed the answer, using the version they actually saw.
Decide who owns the answer and when it can be given. A scope boundary, a live update, and professional judgment each need different support.
Check whether comparable customers can take the next step and still reach someone when their situation warrants it.

faqs.question: When is an FAQ page the right place for an answer?
faqs.answer: Use an FAQ when the answer is useful across several services or situations and customers have a clear route to it. Put buying conditions beside the relevant service or price as well. A contractor comparing a quote should see the scope where they’re deciding whether to sign.

faqs.question: When should we automate replies to common questions?
faqs.answer: Automate retrieval when the answer is stable or the system can read the current, authoritative record. Define who maintains that information and when to send the customer to a person. Try it first on a narrow set of questions and check the replies against real cases, including exceptions.

faqs.question: Who should maintain the answer when several departments use it?
faqs.answer: Give ownership to the team that can change or confirm the underlying promise. Sales may own the standard scope, while dispatch owns the current delivery status. Name who updates the page, quote template and team instructions when the answer changes.
